title: UI: component library browser, compatible-holder filter, and assembly editor

body:
## What to build

Add UI browsing for compatible tool components and an Assembly Builder in the Tool Editor (`crates/ui`), following `crates/ui/AGENTS.md` and the `ui -> app -> flecs` layering rule.

1. **Component Library view** in the Tool Library dock (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_library.rs` and new sub-module):
   - Browse built-in, user-library, and document components by kind (`Inserts`, `Holders`, `Adapters & Extensions`, `Parametric Tools`).
   - Add a "Compatible holders" / "Compatible inserts" filter on any selected component using `compatible_parents` and `compatible_children`.
   - Allow saving a component to or deleting a component from the user library.
2. **Assembly Builder** in the Tool Editor (extending `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_body_assembly_page.rs`):
   - Display the tool's linked component stack (mount -> adapter/extension -> holder -> insert) with port names, Z-rotation, and projection controls.
   - Show derived cutting parameters and gauge length as read-only values driven by the assembly.
   - Offer one-click component swap filtered to compatible components, plus "Edit shared component" (showing how many tools use it) and "Detach to standalone tool".
   - Show an update badge and a "Sync from library" button when a document component differs from the user library.
3. Route every document change through the undoable app commands (Everything Is a Command).

## Notes

- Depends on the document commands and persistence sub-issues of #2452.
- Update structural layout tests (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/page_layout.rs` / `structural.rs`), never snapshot PNGs.

## Done means

- Headless UI tests in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/` verify filtering holders that accept a selected insert, assembling a turning tool from linked components, live update propagation across two tools when editing the shared insert, syncing from the user library, and undo/redo.
- Existing UI layout and behaviour tests stay green without lowering the `#[test]` count.

Part of #2452
